intent: A heading cell naming a column (or a row), with an optional drag and keyboard column resize handle.
typical_uses: One column heading in a TableHeader row
A column whose width the user adjusts

invariants.text: The header styling - mono uppercase labels that do not wrap, a header band height - belongs to TableHead itself, so a TableHead in a body row looks the same as one in TableHeader.

With `resizable` the cell renders a focusable role="separator" handle on its trailing edge. Dragging it, or ArrowLeft / ArrowRight at 12px per press, moves the boundary against the next column so the table's width stays the same. The last column has no neighbour: its handle changes the table's width instead, so the table can end up narrower than its container or wider (the scroll wrapper then scrolls). The first resize writes the current width of every heading in that row inline, switches the table to a fixed layout and pins the table's width to the sum of those widths, unless the table's own style already sets `tableLayout: fixed`: then nothing is written up front, a heading with no inline width of its own counts as zero, and the table shrinks to the columns the resize wrote. A column floors at 72px when it holds text and 32px when it does not; `resizeMinWidth` replaces this column's floor while its own handle is dragged, and when the previous column's handle shrinks it the 72px / 32px floor applies. The last column also stops where the table would drop below its own min-width (960px in the collection view), so the width the handle announces is the one on screen. The handle is named "<heading text> width" ("Column width" when the heading has no text), with the current width in pixels appended once a drag starts or an arrow key moves it.
TableHead is box-sizing border-box, so a width set through style or className includes the cell's padding; a heading holding a role="checkbox" descendant drops its inline-end padding.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Set `resizable` as well - the floor only feeds the resize handle

a11y.by: With `resizable`, table.tsx renders a focusable role="separator" with no aria-valuenow, which WAI-ARIA requires on a focusable separator; the width is only in its aria-label. The heading itself is sound: table.test.tsx asserts two columnheaders and the handle's "Name width" / "Name width, 240 pixels" aria-label

rtl.by: table.tsx applies the pointer's clientX delta and ArrowRight as +12px whatever the direction, while the handle sits on the inline-end edge; in a right-to-left table that edge is on the left, so dragging the handle outward narrows the column

unexposed_parts.reason: An internal span table.tsx renders inside the heading when `resizable` is set; it is not exported, and `resizeMinWidth` is the only prop that reaches it.

good.title: A resizable column with its own floor

bad.title: A floor with no handle
bad.why: Without `resizable` no handle renders, and `resizeMinWidth` has no effect.

capabilities.name: column_resize
capabilities.description: A drag and arrow-key handle on the column's trailing edge that trades width with the next column.
